[b]Ascoiyan Chamber of Commerce[/b]

The Ascoiyans have proven themselves to be a wiley bunch. They desire the resources and technologies of the world entire but are reluctant to let them intrude upon their sacred abodes. The Five Angels of course, have their own share of experiences in such behavior, of nations finally opening up to the world, who want the glamors of progress and industrialization, but without the sickening globalization, cultural mixing, and diversity. The Board of Directors of Almstedt Corporation, in an extraordinary session with the other foreign corporations, have decided that the only way to counteract these anti-market aversions was to dig their heels and wait, wait until the Ascoiyans realize that ever since the billboards and commercial started appearing on their soil, life had never been any better.

To this end, the Five Angels would formally ally with one another and with any sympathetic small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that had been reaping the benefits from the massive influx of cheap imported natural resources. The alliance, formally named the "All-Ascoiyan Chambers of Commerce and Industry", though doing business simply as the Ascoiyan Chamber of Commerce, in order to coordinate business strategy and mitigate damages from Ascoiya's reactionary legislation.

In their first session, a board of trustees would be formed, with Xavier Almstedt of Almstedt Corporation unsurprisingly becoming elected as Chairman and CEO. Other notable figures include Honor Almstedt (Almstedt Corporation), Alessandra Terrasi (Somare S.p.A.), Kang Hongxin (Miwu Group), and Cui Qiang (Qunarco), who would also be elected to positions within the Chamber Board.

Almstedt, acting under pressure from investors, would order the Chamber to organize a list of all international workers able and willing to participate in the Five Angels' lucrative export market to Ascoiya, with the board and its staff devising a complex rotation arrangement to swiftly swap out workers whose residency limits were due to expire. This would be treated as just a stopgap measure though, and the board would agree to lodge a formal complaint with the Ascoiyan government, warning that the laws on foreign residency will paralyze the flow of goods entering Ascoiya and risk damaging its nascent industries. In a keynote speech, senior trustee Cui Qiang would even warn that worker rotation may lead to safety incidents and catastrophic failures as senior experts are forced to be replaced with newcomers to the industry.
